deals.evidence: the firm has acquired a 12.5 percent stake in the club, which has a total value of 4.25 billion euros ($4.58 billion), putting Arctos' investment at 530 million euros
deals.headline: Arctos Partners takes a 12.5% minority stake in PSG from QSI
deals.summary: QSI and Arctos announced a strategic partnership under which Arctos acquired a minority common equity stake in PSG; per a source close to QSI quoted by AFP, 12.5% at a total club value of EUR 4.25bn (EUR 530m). The investment funds growth and real-estate projects (stadium, Poissy training centre). QSI keeps full control.

deals.date_text: June 2025 (capital increase dated 10 June; announced 21 June 2025)
deals.evidence: portent le montant total de souscription à 46 125 000 euros
deals.headline: Kevin Durant becomes a direct minority shareholder of PSG
deals.summary: QSI and Boardroom Sports Holdings, Kevin Durant's personal investment vehicle, signed a share purchase and strategic partnership agreement. Sportune, citing the club's legal filings, reports a capital increase of 2,442,318 new shares subscribed for a total of EUR 46.125m, about 1.6% of the capital, valuing PSG at EUR 2.88bn.

deals.evidence: dont Arctos détient 12,5 % des parts depuis 2023
deals.headline: KKR acquires Arctos Partners, holder of 12.5% of PSG
deals.summary: KKR agreed to acquire 100% of Arctos (USD 1.4bn initial consideration for the whole firm, not for the PSG stake), making it part of KKR Solutions; KKR announced the closing in May 2026 (Business Wire). Arctos has held 12.5% of PSG since 2023, so the stake now sits inside KKR's platform. Indirect change; no PSG shares were transferred.

name: Paris Saint-Germain
notes: Revenue is the club's own 2024-25 figure (EUR 837m, released 28 Oct 2025); the DNCG individual accounts give total non-transfer earnings of EUR 837,011k for the consolidated perimeter (SAS + association + PSG Merchandising + SESE + PSG Handball + SNC Training Center + PSG Judo) and are the source for payroll, operating result (before player trading) and pre-tax result. 2025-26 accounts not yet published (club released 2024-25 in late October). The club's breakdown gives only commercial and matchday; broadcast not stated by the club (DNCG categories differ: broadcasting rights EUR 243,189k, sponsors/advertising EUR 386,560k, gate receipts EUR 78,178k, other EUR 129,084k). QSI's exact current percentage is not stated on any page read: it was 100% before Arctos; Arctos is stated at 12.5% (2026) and Durant at about 1.6% after a June 2025 capital increase, so QSI's stake is left null. The Durant price implies a lower valuation (EUR 2.88bn, per Sportune's reading of the filings) than the Arctos deal (EUR 4.25bn); both are as the pages state. Stadium capacity: the club's overview page states 47,929 seats were installed in the pre-Euro 2016 renovation; its history page says 'around 48,000' and Forbes lists 48,500. Stadium sale/lease talks with the City of Paris reopened April 2026 (steering committee from June 2026); PSG is also studying a new stadium (it held a local steering committee in Massy). No net debt figure stated; Forbes gives debt/value of 1%. France 24 (and RFI's copy of the same AFP story) blocks plain curl (403) but is readable in a browser; the Arctos price and valuation (EUR 530m for 12.5% at EUR 4.25bn) rest on that AFP report of a source close to QSI, so they sit on the deal row while the owner row cites Le Parisien for the 12.5%.
